lean.fidelity_note: The formal theorem proves Lemma 3.1 for one specified family, whereas the paper asserts existence of a suitable family. For every $0<h\le1$, the constructed $F_h$ is smooth, odd and period one; its normalized primitive $P_h$ is smooth, period one and has zero phase mean, with $P_h'=F_h$. There is one $C>0$, chosen before $h$, such that $F_h'(0)=1$, $-Ch\le F_h'\le1$ and $\|F_h\|_\infty\le Ch$. For each integer $j\ge2$, there is $C_j>0$, chosen before $h$ and the phase, such that $\|\partial_s^jF_h\|_\infty\le C_jh^{1-j}$. The exponent uses integer subtraction, so it is negative for $j\ge2$, exactly as in the paper. The specified bump is supported in $[-1/8,1/8]$, inside the interval allowed by the proof. Phase mean means integration over $[0,1]$; the primitive is normalized by subtracting that mean, not by fixing its value at zero. The formula is defined outside the admissible width range, but the theorem asserts these properties only for $0<h\le1$. The stronger verdict concerns the identified family and its uniform estimates; it does not assert spatial periodicity after evaluation at an arbitrary real wave vector.

statements.markdown:
**Lemma 3.1.** There are odd smooth $1$-periodic functions $F_h$, $0<h\le1$, with zero-mean primitives $P_h$, such that $$F_h'(0)=1,\qquad -Ch\le F_h'\le1,\qquad
 \left\lVert F_h\right\rVert_\infty\le Ch,\qquad
 \left\lVert\partial_s^jF_h\right\rVert_\infty\le C_jh^{1-j}\quad(j\ge2).$$
